doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Freddie Green and Manny's golf day with Clark Terry
summary: At Manny's annual musicians' golf outing Freddie Green talked to him and he made a bet with Clark Terry; later a limousine meeting with Terry.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What kind of fellas, for the Basie band — was it Lester Young or let’s see Buddy Tate, those fellas?
You mean playing in these places?

I never seen the guitar player, Green, Freddie Green. But I became — in the place I didn’t see him, maybe he was playing there but I didn’t notice it. But later on we had Manny’s, it’s a music — it’s still there I think Manny. He’s dead but his son runs it. And they used to have a golf game every year and they’d invite all the big musicians who either deal with the store or hang out there, I don’t know. Well I was invited a couple of times. And the one time I was playing and Freddie Green was there too. He didn’t play, but we were in the golf game, in the tournament. And after, Manny would have all the instruments, not your instruments, he’d just have them there if you felt like picking it up. So I was playing, and that’s how Freddie Green started to talk to me, he told me he says if my son wants to take a lesson I’m going to send him to you. He liked me. And well the other part of that, I’m not a great golfer. At that time I just played for fun. And Clark Terry was on my foursome. And I knew Clark. So Clark says, “Let’s me and you have a bet” he says, “I’ll bet you I’ll beat you.” So I says, “Well I don’t play.” He says “I don’t play.” We ruined the foursome, the other two guys were mad. We were behind trees. So at the end, Manny’s got a motion picture you know, like a 16 millimeter or something, of the end of the game. It was in the Engineer’s Club in Glen Cove, well it’s right in Long Island.

Well I don’t know if it’s Glen Cove or what, but it was the Engineer’s Country Club. Manny would hire it out for one day a week, nobody else but musicians, from morning to night we’d go there, they’d put us in the dressing room, they’d take our shoes and shine our shoes, when we come back out. It was ridiculous. And I’d have breakfast. So we’d go out and at the ninth hole he’d have hamburgers or hot dogs. At four or five o’clock when you finished the eighteen, they had a cocktail party. After the cocktail party we’d go in and get all dressed up, and go back into the dining room and that’s where all the © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
instruments were set up, and we’d eat in there, the whole day. So at the end of this thing, he’s got — I beat him, I don’t know, I beat him by one stroke. It was terrible.
And he’s flipping a quarter to me, and I’d catch the thing. So I bet Clark Terry.

Oh he’s a beautiful guy. And then at Flip’s birthday party not so long ago, his 80th birthday, and oddly enough me and my wife got into this limousine, to pick us up at the airport, and he come in. So I told him I says the only thing I can beat you at is at golf. I ought to call him up right before we die and tell him to come on out and play golf. He probably took lessons.
